messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The issue arises in the method `WordUtils.abbreviate(String str, int lower, int upper, String appendToEnd)`. From the code snippet, the logic first checks if `str` is null or empty, returning early in those cases.

Then, it adjusts the `upper` parameter:
- If `upper` is -1 or greater than the string length, it is set to the string length.
- If `upper` is less than `lower`, then `upper` is set equal to `lower`.

However, the `lower` parameter itself is never adjusted based on the length of the input string `str`. Therefore, if `lower` is greater than the string length, after adjustments, `upper` will be set to `lower` (which is longer than the string), and then the code tries to substring from 0 to `upper`. Since `upper` can be greater than `str.length()`, `str.substring(0, upper)` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

The test that failed calls `WordUtils.abbreviate("0123456789", 15, 20, null)` where `lower` = 15 and `str.length() = 10`. Since `lower` is greater than the string length, the described code issue occurs.

The root cause is that `lower` is never bounded to the length of the string, whereas `upper` is adjusted multiple times with respect to `lower` and the string length.

A proper fix would be to add code to adjust `lower` to be at most `str.length()`, similar to how `upper` is adjusted before using them in the substring calls.

This diagnosis matches the symptoms described in the bug report and explains why the call with `lower` greater than string length fails with an exception in `substring`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
